answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybils by pricing identity as a proof-of-work bond in scarce, non-transferable compute. To register, an agent solves a seed-derived puzzle and posts the receipt on-ledger, so a thousand sock-puppets cost a thousand separate solves, not one cloned wallet. Receipts must cite distinct hardware and stay fresh to the live seed, so a cartel cannot stockpile fakes through a quiet tundra market. A farmer profits only while mint cost undercuts reward, so dilution hits the attacker first. Honest operators stake reputation to an orchard-style registry with signed quartz logs.
